decoder.description: json: one JSON object per line; regex: text lines read with pattern; plain: no structure.

fields.description: json decoder: where each standard field is, as candidate JSON paths (first present wins; dots walk into objects).

message.description: Message text; required by the json decoder.

time.description: Entry time (RFC 3339 string or epoch seconds/milliseconds).

hidden.description: json decoder: fields (globs on dotted paths) never shown on the stream nor searched, only in the hidden fields of zoom, e.g. ["kubernetes.*"].

layout.description: Layout used to draw these lines: a file name of layouts/ without extension.

level_from.description: json and regex decoders: raise the level from another field, e.g. the HTTP status. It never lowers the level.

field.description: Field whose value decides the level, e.g. status: a group of pattern (regex), or a JSON path or a field extracted by a transform (json).

map.description: Glob on the value to level (error, warn, info, debug), tried longest glob first, e.g. {"5*": error, "4*": warn}. The line takes the more severe of its level and the matched one; no match keeps its level.

levels.description: Extra spellings of each level in these logs (case ignored), e.g. {error: ["50", FATAL]}. Common spellings are known already.

match.description: Containers read with this format. Formats are tried in file name order; the first match wins. No match section: every container.

containers.description: Globs on the container name, e.g. [nginx]. Empty: any container.

repos.description: Globs on the repository name, e.g. ["payment-*"]. Empty: any repository.

mute.description: Loggers whose lines are hidden (connection pool state, resource snapshots…): they never reach the logs screen, where M shows them again.

keep.description: Levels shown even from a muted logger, e.g. [error]. Default: none, every line of a muted logger is hidden.

loggers.description: Logger names as the lines write them, case-sensitive: exact (com.example.pool.Pool) or a prefix ending in * (com.example.metrics.*).

pattern.description: regex decoder: Go regular expression with named groups; time, level, logger, thread, message, trace_id, app and pid are standard fields, other groups become extra fields. message is required.

time_format.description: regex decoder: Go reference layout of the time group, e.g. 02/Jan/2006:15:04:05 -0700. Default RFC 3339.

max_bytes.description: Values longer than this many bytes are left as they are (the regular expression costs about 50 µs per KiB). At least 1. Default 16384.

max_fields.description: At most this many fields extracted per line; the rest stays in the raw view. At least 1. Default 64.

pair_pattern.description: Go regular expression reading one pair of a pairs group, with the groups key and value, e.g. '(?P<key>[\w.-]+): (?P<value>[^;]*);?'. The matches must cover the group except white space, otherwise the group is kept whole. Default: key=value separated by white space.

pairs.description: Groups of pattern holding key=value text, e.g. [before, after]: each pair becomes a field; empty values are left out.

pattern.description: Go regular expression with a group named after the field, e.g. (?P<message>…): when it matches, the group becomes the field's value; otherwise nothing changes. Other named groups become fields of the line (standard ones fill their field when the JSON left it empty); time and stack groups are not allowed.

transform.description: json decoder: keep part of a standard field's value and extract fields from it, by field, e.g. {message: {pattern: '- (?P<message>.*?) -'}}.

version.description: Structure version of this file; must be 1.
